description: ST I q.19 a.1's argument, typed with forms: whatever has intellect is in act through an intelligible form (STMT-INTELLECT-HAS-INTELLIGIBLE-FORM); an inclination follows every form (STMT-EVERY-FORM-HAS-INCLINATION); an inclination following an intelligible form is will (STMT-INTELLIGIBLE-INCLINATION-IS-WILL). Derives STMT-WILL-FOLLOWS-INTELLECT, an underived leaf of 18 root routes. Discharges obligations A and B of the AQUINAS-INTELLECTUAL-APPETITE-TO-WILL candidate as explicit typed premises (form-relative orientation at the level of power, no exercise or passivity) and states C as an explicit recognition bridge; it does not identify natural with cognitive appetite, since a being with only a natural form has its inclination and no will in the controls. All three premises stay open.
